caveats: Counts describe captured action evidence, not independent proof of user benefit.
Failure rates are provider-reported tool-result signals where available; missing outcome structure is not success.
Recent windows are adoption-sensitive and can legitimately differ from all-time counts.
Zero captured agent use is not enough to remove operator-only surfaces; those rows carry an operator-only caveat.
claim: Polylogue can compare agent affordance usage across normalized action evidence without summing unlike tool-name spellings or provider-specific call shapes.
non_claim: This is not a human-quality utility evaluation of any particular tool family. It measures captured usage evidence, failure signals, and coverage gaps; usefulness still requires qualitative review of session context and outcomes.
